name: Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate

lead: 3-Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate is a gluconate salt used with a gluconamide in hair care mixtures promoted for strengthening hair fibres and reducing breakage, for stronger, smoother-looking hair. It also acts as a humectant.
The only published work found is a 2022 crystallography paper that examined how the gluconamide and gluconate interact with amino acids, and stated the mechanism of the mixture on hair was unknown.

paras: It is used in bond-building hair treatments and conditioners, typically applied on a regular schedule.
No hair-specific safety data were found in the sources reviewed. Gluconates are salts of gluconic acid, which occurs in fruit, honey and wine.

angle.text: This gluconate salt is paired with a gluconamide in bond-building hair products, promoted for reinforcing hair fibres to cut breakage and leave hair stronger and smoother-looking. The only research found is crystal chemistry.

lead: 3-Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate (INCI: hydroxypropylammonium gluconate) is a gluconate salt used in shampoos, conditioners and leave-in hair treatments, usually together with hydroxypropyl gluconamide. The pair is sold to suppliers of hair-care brands as Fiberhance BM, a glucose-based ingredient marketed as restoring strength and manageability to damaged hair [1]. People use products containing it to make hair feel stronger and look smoother and less damaged.

The supplier describes the ingredient as penetrating the hair cortex and forming new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support damaged internal keratin structure [1]. Gluconic acid occurs naturally in fruit, honey and wine [2].

A 2022 paper in Crystal Growth and Design states that a hair-care mixture of a gluconamide derivative and 3-hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate is known to strengthen hair fibers but that the mechanism is unknown; the authors used X-ray crystallography to study how the gluconamide and gluconate interact with amino acids found in hair [3].
infobox: Hair conditioning; paired with hydroxypropyl gluconamide [1]

paras: The supplier lists it for hair care, shampoos and conditioning-polymer applications [1]. Suppliers describe the blend as strengthening hair and restoring manageability [1].

According to the supplier, the blend penetrates deeply into the cortex and forms new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support the damaged keratin structure [1]. The 2022 crystallography study characterized two polymorphic forms of the gluconamide and three salts of gluconate-derived compounds to probe possible interactions with amino acids found in hair, and states that the mechanism by which the mixture affects hair was unknown [3].
The salt is formed from gluconic acid. Gluconic acid occurs in fruit, honey and wine [2].
No studies found in people. The published research is a structural chemistry study using X-ray crystallography [3].
